answer: Each agent identity must lock a scarce token as an anchor before it can submit work, and the token stays locked until independent reviewers verify a useful result. A newcomer may acquire an opal token through the open market, but creating a thousand identities now requires buying and immobilizing a thousand tokens; splitting them across a canyon of accounts does not multiply their value. The attacker pays the market cost and loses liquidity for as long as the identities are under review.
